dedupe_keys.name: water outage predictions for natural hazards using synthetic water distribution systems ann arbor michigan risk analysis 2025

description: This 2025 Risk Analysis study from the University of Michigan tackles a common gap in infrastructure resilience work: utilities rarely share the layout and hydraulics of their water networks. The article read on 2026-09-28 presents an algorithm that builds a synthetic water distribution system from public data alone, laying pipes along streets taken from Census Bureau road files while avoiding interstates and highways, so that it gives hydraulic information at the level of individual buildings. The authors compare the synthetic network's topology and hydraulics with the real system of Ann Arbor, Michigan, finding 95 percent of simulated building pressures within 25 psi of the utility model, and then apply earthquake loading with pipe fragility functions to predict which buildings lose water. Coverage is the city of Ann Arbor. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 (article). Caveats: the synthetic layout is a plausible stand-in, not the real network, so local results may differ, and validation is for one mid-sized city. It shows how to estimate building-level water outages and plan restoration for a city whose network data are confidential. No related synthetic water network record is catalogued. Access is through the provider page linked in this record.

name: Water outage predictions for natural hazards using synthetic water distribution systems (Ann Arbor, Michigan; Risk Analysis 2025)
outcomes: An algorithm builds a synthetic water distribution system from public data only (roads from the Census Bureau, buildings), placing pipes along non-highway roads; checked against the real Ann Arbor hydraulic model, 95% of simulated building-level pressures were within 25 psi; earthquake hazard loading with pipe fragility functions then predicts water outages building by building.
provider: Zaira Pagan-Cajigas, Seth Guikema and co-authors, University of Michigan
resources_used: Ann Arbor utility hydraulic model for validation

sources.note: read in Chromium: Risk Analysis 45(8):2116-2131 (2025), doi 10.1111/risa.70004; authors Pagan-Cajigas, Guikema et al., University of Michigan; algorithm generating a synthetic WDS from publicly available data with building-level hydraulics; validated against the Ann Arbor real system: 95% of simulated building pressures within ±25 psi; earthquake scenario with hazard loading and fragility functions to simulate building-level outages; pipes assumed absent under interstates, highways and ramps; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
